data.name: Deadnaut
data.detailed_description:
Deadnaut is Screwfly Studios' second game and follow up to cult hit, Zafehouse: Diaries.

Deadnauts, so named because they’re unlikely to return, must explore, investigate and fight their way through the derelict ships of dead civilisations. Every mission is unique and no two locations are the same. Each ship contains mysterious enemies and hostile security systems. Manage your Deadnauts' skills, talents, relationships and flaws - and you might get them out alive.

Features

  • Squad-based tactics: Control five complex characters as they explore, investigate and fight their way through each mission
  • Character generation: Create back stories for your team, mould their relationships and equip them well
  • Every game is unique: Dynamically-generated missions and campaigns ensure no two mysteries are the same
  • Flexible and complex: Adapt to your situation with an arsenal of weapons and shields, or use stealth, hacking and sensors to move unnoticed
  • Out of control: Deadnauts have their own fears, motivations and dispositions. Stay in charge, keep in contact, don’t let them out of your sight

There are many ways to play Deadnaut. You can focus on combat and offense with a heavily-armed crew, or go quietly with sensors, cloaks and shields. Use randomly generated Deadnauts, or fine-tune your crew with the character generator. It’s your call.

Deadnaut is a challenging game. Not all strategies will work all the time. Instead, you'll need to equip your squad with the right tools, maximise your Deadnauts' respective talents, and adjust your approach when things go wrong.

About Screwfly Studios

We're a two-man developer based in Australia, dedicated to creating deep, innovative strategy games for PC. Deadnaut is the follow-up to Screwfly's debut title, Zafehouse: Diaries, which is also available on Steam.

reviews.review:
I loved this game's theme, atmosphere and presentation. Unfortunately, the actual gameplay just didn't work out for me.

The game would have benefitted greatly from even a simple tutorial. Right now all you get is a lengthy manual. Some controls aren't obvious, and you won't survive unless you have a good grip on the game's mechanics. In my first game, it took me a while to even figure out what killed most of my team.

The way your crew all have personality flaws makes it sound like it would be challenging yet fun to work around them, much like in Jagged Alliance. Unfortunately, in practice the dialogue is repetitive and your team members have very little personality. Some flaws are crippling and make the team member practically unusable. For example, one will have your team member occasionally disobey orders, which has a good chance of getting them killed as they randomly wander into a room full of enemies; another will have them panic or go berserk almost every time they take damage; a third will make the team member hated by all his buddies, which will hinder the performance of the entire team.

The game is also very RNG-heavy. There are various types of enemy, each with specific strengths and weaknesses to certain damage types. But if you actually want to get weapons with the appropriate damage type, you have to find it during a mission and hope it's the right one. And having the correct weapons and armour is crucial, as, once a fight begins, there is little in the way of tactics beyond concentrating your teams firepower. There is a Stealth skill, but I found it virtually useless in practice.

Your team doesn't get to improve their skills between missions, and there is no meta-progression. It would have gone a long way towards making the game enjoyable on repeated runs.

While the environments are appropriately spooky, there is not much variation among them. There scenery is also repetitive, mostly just dead bodies, doors and computer terminals, plus the occasional teleporter. The enemies are all depicted as red dots - assigning an icon (like the skull-and-dagger used for your team members) to each of the various enemy types would have helped.

I could have lived with some of the mentioned flaws, but when put together they make the game too frustrating for me to enjoy.

Thankfully, the game eventually got a sequel called Deadnaut: Signal Lost, which is a much better game, though closer to a traditional roguelike because it's turn-based and you control only a single character.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows XP
  • Processador: Intel Core 2 Duo 2.2GHz or AMD Athlon 64 X2 5000
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA or AMD/ATI graphics card with 1GB RAM, with support for Direct3D 9 and Shader Model 3
  • DirectX: Versão 9.0c
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 250 MB de espaço livre
  • Placa de som: DirectX compatible sound card

mac_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo: macOS 10.7 - 10.14
  • Processador: Intel Core 2 Duo
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA or AMD/ATI graphics card with 1GB RAM and Shader Model 3 support
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 250 MB de espaço livre

linux_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo: Ubuntu 12.04
  • Processador: Intel Core 2 Duo
  • Memória: 2 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA or AMD/ATI graphics card with 1GB RAM and Shader Model 3 support
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 250 MB de espaço livre
  • Notas adicionais: Other Linux distributions should work, however they are not officially supported.
